finding.claim: scrub_css emits identifier values unescaped for non-shorthand properties such as cursor and list-style. A CSS-escaped identifier that decodes to url(...) is not a :url token on the first parse, so the url check passes. The decoded text is reparsed as a real url() token and written to the output style attribute. Confirmed by reading Crass 1.0.6 source; not executed.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled style attribute on any element Loofah sanitizes, for example Loofah.html5_fragment(input).scrub!(:strip) or Loofah::Helpers.sanitize. Payload: cursor: u\72l\28http\3a\2f\2fzexample\2eorg\2fpath\2fimg\2epng\29
finding.sink: Sanitized style attribute containing cursor:url(http://zexample.org/path/img.png), which makes the victim browser fetch a remote resource. The sanitizer is meant to strip url() entirely. Impact is remote load or tracking, not script execution.

trace.note: scrub_css_attribute reads node.attributes['style'], the attacker input
Crass.parse_properties tokenizes the CSS; the escaped identifier becomes one :ident whose :value is unescaped to url(http:...)
url_flags check inspects only top-level child node types; the ident is not :url or :bad_url, so it passes
keyword = child[:value] takes the unescaped value
the shorthand guard only covers background, border, margin and padding, so cursor and list-style return the ident without any keyword filter
propstring 'cursor:url(http:...)' is reparsed; Crass yields a :url token; only .first is kept, which truncates extra declarations but not the url
Crass::Parser.stringify emits the url raw into the output

finding.guards_checked: url_flags node-type check at line 104 (runs on the pre-reparse tree only); shorthand keyword filter at 127 (does not cover cursor or list-style); ALLOWED_CSS_FUNCTIONS at 122 (not applied to reparsed text); .first at 141 (blocks extra declarations, not url); no re-validation after reparse; allowed_uri? (not applied to CSS).

finding.claim: allowed_uri? returns true for javascript&#58alert(1). CGI.unescapeHTML only decodes entities that end in ';' (Ruby cgi/util.rb:97), and URI_PROTOCOL_REGEX (scrub.rb:17) requires a literal ':' after the scheme, so the scheme check is skipped. Browsers decode numeric references without a semicolon in attribute values. Confirmed for the allowed_uri? API by reading. The DOM-path exploit (Loofah::Helpers.sanitize, html4/libxml2) is PLAUSIBLE and not executed: it depends on libxml2 writing href values with '&' unescaped.
finding.source: Attribute value of href, src, action, cite or other ATTR_VAL_IS_URI attributes. Direct API input: javascript:alert(1). DOM input: x, which libxml2 decodes once to javascript:alert(1).
finding.sink: Attribute kept in sanitized output; if serialized raw, the browser decodes &#58 to ':' and the link becomes a javascript: URL (XSS on click). Likely not reachable on the HTML5/Gumbo path, which escapes '&' in attributes.

trace.note: CGI.unescapeHTML only decodes ';'-terminated refs, so &#58alert is left as-is
URI_PROTOCOL_REGEX requires a literal ':' after [a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*; the input has '&' there, so the regex does not match
scrub_uri_attribute keeps the attribute when allowed_uri? is true
force_correct_attribute_escaping! only handles space and double-quote, so '&' is not escaped here

finding.guards_checked: CONTROL_CHARACTERS strip (line 172-173): irrelevant to the entity form. : replacement (line 174): only the named form. PROTOCOL_SEPARATOR (safelist.rb:986) handles &#58 without ';' but is reached only after URI_PROTOCOL_REGEX matches, which it does not. Case 08 invariant (validate after every decode) is violated.
